public_rationale: This is an open-ended forecast. The available leasing and posted-price records do not establish a decisive industry-wide overbuild event. They also cannot rule out a later overbuild. No event meeting the early-resolution rule was established by October 28, so neither support nor contradiction is warranted.
limitations: Leased space is not the same as utilized AI compute.
Posted GPU prices are not realized transaction prices or operator profits.
The absence of a deadline makes conclusive contradiction especially difficult.

statement.excerpt: In other words, I believe we are now in an inevitable overbuild situation, one with no neat, tidy Dot-Com Bubble-style exit story.

from_speaker: now in an inevitable overbuild situation
no neat, tidy Dot-Com Bubble-style exit story
our_interpretation: The surrounding discussion predicts that the current AI data-center buildout will eventually produce capacity that paying compute demand cannot economically support.
An overbuild means sustained, material excess operational capacity with associated investment losses, rather than temporary construction delays or occasional idle equipment.
The comparison with the dot-com era suggests stranded assets or losses without an easy later recovery. It supplies no precise historical recovery benchmark.
I believe does not remove the firm commitment conveyed by inevitable.
No deadline is stated, so no terminal evaluation date is imposed.
criteria.support_condition: Evidence connects the current buildout to sustained, widespread excess operational AI capacity and material stranded-asset losses, with no economically successful redeployment sufficient to explain away the alleged overbuild.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A completed assessment of the identified buildout establishes durable economic absorption or successful redeployment without material excess capacity and losses. Short-term shortages alone cannot refute an unlimited-horizon forecast.
